Roles and Responsibilities

This section of the staffing plan describes the roles on the project, including the boundaries and responsibilities within which team resources operate. Agile project teams are typically comprised of the following roles:

  • Stakeholders - any person with an interest in the project that is not the Product Owner, Scrum Master or Development Team. This could be an end-user of the product, the sponsor, subject matter experts or members of other departments.
  • Scrum Team - those directly involved with the project broken into the following roles:
    • Product Owner
    • Scrum Master
    • Development Team

Agile teams have defined roles that are treated more as a boundary since teams are staffed cross-functionally. The Development Team consists of members having all the expertise and competencies needed to deliver without material help from outside the team and are self-organized to manage their own efforts in achieving the outlined goals.

For more information on the responsibilities and characteristics of the Scrum team please refer to the Product Owner, Scrum Master and Development Team roles directly.

Reporting Relationships

As there is no hierarchy between any of these roles (Product Owner, Scrum Master, Development Team), there are no direct reporting relationships in the traditional sense. Rather, Agile dictates that the team operates in a collaborative fashion to provide a shared vision and optimize their teamwork in order to deliver the outlined goals as efficiently as possible. The Scrum team members plan, develop, deliver and improve together.

Scrum ceremonies such as the daily Scrum, sprint planning, sprint retrospective and sprint review are put in place to enable this relationship of information sharing and collaboration among team members. These meetings enable all of the roles to be effective without relying on standard reporting relationships.

Staff Management

Stable Scrum teams are important in order to maximize efficiency and nuture the maturity of team relationships. The Scrum team should be involved in any staffing decisions as the team is supposed to be self-sufficient. The key piece of staff management is making sure the Scrum Master facilitates and coaches all members of the team on Agile principles so they can avoid impediments that would prevent progress.

Onboarding and Release Timing

This section of the staffing plan describes order and timing of assembling teams and/or when each team member will be included in the initiative. Typically, entire teams are assembled at one time to provide stability and reduce the amount of time spent ramping up or down.

Usually this includes description and timing of onboarding activities at the start of the project and handover activities at the conclusion during release.
To describe how the roles and responsibilities, reporting relationships, and staff management will be addressed and structured.

May be less crucial for projects with a small number of team members that are highly focused on the project and closely working together. For example, three individuals working on a short term project who are fully dedicated and jointly available.
